title: The Missing Origin — partial content provenance across research, implementation, community reports, and Commons

sources.title: Enhanced image forensics through partial C2PA-based provenance information
sources.observed_claim: An image can have valid partial content credentials reflecting later processing while prior provenance remains unknown.
sources.limitations: The paper evaluates a forensic strategy; it does not prove relationships among ROOT0 artifacts or that every partial manifest is fraudulent.

sources.title: Verifying Provenance of Digital Media: Why the C2PA Specifications Fall Short
sources.observed_claim: Authors report shortcomings in the security guarantees of the studied C2PA protocols and caution against high-stakes reliance.
sources.limitations: A research team's analysis, not a universal demonstration that all provenance manifests are invalid.

sources.title: Authenticated Contradictions from Desynchronized Provenance and Watermarking
sources.observed_claim: Authors demonstrate a scenario in which separately valid cryptographic metadata and watermark indications can be contradictory.
sources.limitations: This is a specified cross-layer mismatch scenario, not evidence of any particular producer's intent.

sources.title: Content Authenticity Initiative — c2pa-rs
sources.observed_claim: Open-source Rust SDK provides operations to sign, embed, parse, and validate C2PA content credentials.
sources.limitations: Repository implementation documents capabilities; no deployment, commit date, or adoption path is inferred from the present listing.

sources.title: C2PA public specification repository
sources.observed_claim: Public technical specification is maintained in a separate standards repository.
sources.limitations: Specification and SDK are related ecosystem sources, not independent roots for the same standards claim.

sources.title: Content Credentials Problem — r/ElevenLabs
sources.observed_claim: A user reports different apparent content-credential behavior across voice-export workflows; a commenter proposes a rendering-path explanation.
sources.limitations: Neither export behavior nor the suggested technical explanation was independently replicated.

sources.title: Content Credentials? — r/photoshop
sources.observed_claim: Participants discuss content credentials appearing on media and concerns about metadata survival after editing.
sources.limitations: Comments are not a controlled test of specific software and file formats.

sources.title: Commons:AI-generated media
sources.observed_claim: Guidance encourages identifying the AI engine and prompter, documenting prompts, and categorizing AI-generated works.
sources.limitations: Declared attribution is distinct from cryptographically verified provenance; guidelines do not prove compliance.

sources.title: Commons:Machine-readable data
sources.observed_claim: Commons describes machine-readable metadata approaches and the limits of free-text file descriptions.
sources.limitations: Machine-readable does not imply truthful or cryptographically authenticated origin.

convergence_observations.finding: Recent operations can be documented while earlier ancestry remains absent; descriptive metadata may supply a declared account, but is a separate evidentiary tier.
Passing a manifest validation step should not be collapsed into a claim of complete provenance or content truth.
Community reports of inconsistent credential preservation are compatible with research on incomplete histories; no direct causal relation is established.
SDK and specification are related materials, not independent corroborating witnesses for standards claims.

independent_origin_policy: Do not count different posts, formats, pages, or implementations as independent origins solely because they have different URLs. Explicit relationship between specification and SDK is tracked.
methodological_limits: Dates on published research and dated community posts are public source dates; no first-origin timestamp is inferred.
A Reddit report is testimony of a user's experience, not proof of actual exported metadata.
Not a plagiarism, adoption, infringement, conspiracy, collusion, or causal transmission finding.
No specific ROOT0 document was shown ingested or reused by these third parties.
